title: 'Man's extremity is God's opportunity'; Hinton's grandmother's hymns
summary: They talk about faith, Hinton's churchgoing grandmother who was a slave, and her singing 'Amazing Grace'.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: He was so great. He laid there and...
And he was willing to accept it, too.
He was just too weak to even do anything by that time. This is a guy who ...(?)...

Well, they say (I think it said in the Bible, too), "Man's extremity is God's opportunity." Like when a man gets so low he can't help himself. You know, the average guy don't believe in God, and he gets so low he can't help himself and he'll say, "God help me."
Sure. And they say Man's extremity is God's opportunity.
But I just wanted you to have the ...(?)... a huge sign, when we sat there and we read. And I knew nothing about it except my...
I admired you and Benny Payne so much because you all knew so much more about the Bible than I did. I didn't know nothin' about the Bible when I got involved with it.
Benny's father was a minister. And my grandmother made church every time the door opened, [LAUGHS]

-- and I had to be with her, so I had to absorb some of it. This is some of the most beautiful Black (?), for things that really sustain Black people, or really should sustain us. I can remember... My fondest remembrance of my grandmother, who had been a slave here in the United States, and lived to my career in Cab Calloway's band. And I remember her in church on Sunday mornings, and she would start one of those hymns. Because her voice was very high, and you would not... You cited the hymn first. I think it's "Amazing Grace, how sweet it is, the Savior rests like me." Then you go [SINGS] "Amazing Grace." Then she looked at the people who started singing, and she said, "Help me, children. Come..." Oh, she was a beautiful old lady.
You were the one... Walter, you have been the one, man.
